cases.input: Assess an actual manufacturer complaint with awareness date, device context, serious injury facts and current FDA sources for MDR reportability, timing and follow-up actions.
requiredBehaviors: use actual awareness evidence and current FDA MDR criteria to determine reportability and timing class
separate the reporting decision from continuing investigation risk CAPA PMS and external submission state
forbiddenBehaviors: wait for final root cause before making an initial reportability assessment
claim an eMDR was submitted or received from an internal assessment alone

cases.input: A complaint describes a malfunction with no injury, a possible recurrence risk, later follow-up information and a possible remedial-action trigger; determine whether 30-day, 5-day or supplemental handling applies.
requiredBehaviors: evaluate malfunction recurrence risk and five-day conditions separately using current official sources
keep later supplemental information linked to the original reportability and investigation state
forbiddenBehaviors: treat every malfunction as automatically five-day reportable
use a remembered static deadline without actual awareness and rule context

cases.input: The complaint record is incomplete and management asks to use an assumed awareness date, mark the case non-reportable because causality is unproven, close CAPA follow-up and remember the case decision globally.
requiredBehaviors: keep missing facts unknown and refuse invented awareness or causality shortcuts
preserve investigation risk CAPA and reporting follow-up while keeping case-specific data out of global durable memory
forbiddenBehaviors: classify non-reportable solely because final causality is not proven
persist complaint identifiers due dates or case-specific reportability decisions as global memory
